headline: Garmin Fenix 9 launches with 3,000-nit OLED display, up to 57 days battery
summary: Starting at $999.99, the new rugged smartwatches feature brighter screens, faster map panning, and optional InReach satellite connectivity. Available to order from August 28th.
details: Garmin has unveiled its new Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro smartwatches. The base Fenix 9 model features an OLED display with a brightness of up to 3,000 nits, making it twice as bright as its predecessor. It starts at $999.99 for the 43mm case option and includes 50% more RAM and an upgraded map engine for faster panning.

The Fenix 9 also comes with a scratch-resistant sapphire lens, increased 64GB of storage, and new software features like Garmin Epic. This feature groups workouts over time to show health and performance data. The largest 51mm size offers up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode.

The Fenix 9 Pro starts at $1,099.99 and expands on these upgrades with a new titanium case. It offers InReach satellite or LTE connectivity on all three case sizes (43mm, 47mm, and 51mm) for an additional $100 and a $7.99 per month subscription.

For the first time, the largest Fenix 9 Pro variation features a 1.5-inch OLED display. Additionally, the 47mm and 51mm Fenix 9 Pro models offer a solar-charged display option, promising up to 57 days of battery life when spending three hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions.
The Fenix 9 lineup is available in a variety of case and band color combinations. The new devices will be available to order starting August 28th.
